newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian conglomerate reports 1996 profit slump.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian conglomerate reports 1996 profit slump.

text.p: Conglomerate Ireland Blyth on Monday reported a 60 percent slump in its profit before tax to 20.1 million rupees ($995,000) for the year ended 31 December 1996, from 50.3 million rupees in 1995.

Company officials said turnover rose by 11.5 percent to 3.17 billion rupees in 1996 from 2.85 billion rupees in 1995 but profit after tax crashed by 78 percent to 8.74 million rupees in 1996 from 39.6 million rupees one year earlier.
"1996 has been a year of transition and the board (of directors) is confident in the company's performance in the short to medium term," the officials said.
They blamed difficult conditions in the local trading sector for the worse financial results and said re-organisation was already under way in the company.
They saw higher contribution towards profitability and growth from the conglomerate's growing regional presence in Zimbabwe, Tanzania and Seychelles in the tourism and environmental sectors.
